input:
Our SoC is hitting thermal shutdown during heavy PCIe traffic. The root cause appears to be an MSI interrupt storm from a misconfigured PCIe endpoint. The endpoint is generating thousands of MSIs per second, and each one causes a GIC SPI that the kernel is servicing. This heats up the CPU cluster and eventually triggers emergency thermal shutdown.

/proc/interrupts (sampled over 1 second):
 128:   45201   44987   45102   45330   GICv3  160 Level   pcie-msi-0000:01:00.0

dmesg:
[  300.100] pcieport 0000:00:01.0: PME: Spurious native interrupt!
[  300.101] irq 128: nobody cared (try booting with irqpoll)
[  300.500] thermal_zone0: critical temperature reached (105000 mC), shutting down

ftrace irq_handler_entry:
 irq_handler_entry: irq=128 name=pcie-msi handler=0xffffffc0104a2000
  duration: 2.1us  (x45000/sec = ~95ms/sec CPU time)

GIC ITS device table shows the endpoint mapped to a single collection targeting CPU0-3 round-robin. How do we stop the storm without disabling the device entirely?
